result.reasoning:
REFUTED: the report's load-bearing premise — that `PanelSet.dates` has a 60-day warm-up trimmed off it — is false for the only configuration `idea_search.py` can run. `trim` is 0, and at trim=0 the line as written is exactly correct.

1) `warmed_view` (AlphaCube `src/alphacube/research.py:82-86`) computes `d0 = max(0, base.d0 - warmup)` and returns `trim = base.d0 - d0`, i.e. `trim = min(base.d0, warmup)`. `base.d0 = searchsorted(store.dates, start)` (`store.py:196-201`). So trim is 60 only if the store holds >=60 trading days *before* the requested start.

2) `idea_search.py:63` hard-codes `START, END, SPLIT = "20180102", "20230807", "20220101"` and line 64 hard-codes the store path — there is no `--start` override. And 20180102 is the store's FIRST trading day: `partura/splits.py:27` says "The production view of the AlphaCube store: 20180102..20251231, 1942 trading days", AlphaCube `docs/HANDOFF.md:65` says "全市场视图 20180102~20251231 = 1942 天 × 5220 只"; the `incremental/` segments are 追加段 (appended, i.e. later — the base `minute/` segment's 2092 days extend past 2025-12-31 into 2026, they are not pre-2018 days).

3) Direct empirical proof from the repo's own logs: `PanelSet.compute` prints `(+{self.trim} warm-up)` (`partura/panels.py:364-365`). Every one of the 59 such lines in `/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/logs` reads `1942d x 5220s (+0 warm-up)` — and those runs did request a warm-up (e.g. `logs/F113_nested_tsmax_demean_S1_chain.log:5` is `(+0 warm-up)` while `configs/F113_nested_tsmax_demean.yaml:17` is `warmup: 60`; every config in `configs/` sets `warmup: 60` and every script defaults to 60). `grep -rho "(+[0-9]* warm-up)" logs episodes runs studies | sort | uniq -c` → `59 (+0 warm-up)`, zero other values. If the store had pre-2018 days these would all print `(+60 warm-up)`.

4) Reproduction (see `reproduction`): with the real `alphacube.research.warmed_view` against a real `CubeStore` whose calendar starts 20180102, `warmed_view(store, "20180102", "20230807", 60) -> trim=0`; the same call on a control store starting 20170501 gives `trim=60`. Running the real `cross_valid_count` kernel and the exact lines 99-100 at trim=0, the current formula and the reporter's "corrected" formula agree on **0.000% of cells** — identical flag counts for every listing date (name listed on view day 30: 246/2087 days flagged by BOTH; day 100: 316 by BOTH; day 400: 616 by BOTH). The reporter's headline "flagged on 0 of 400 view days" is produced only by their own hard-coded `WARM, VIEW = 60, 400` in `tmp/review/screen-ops-universe/t3_untradable_reward.py:44`, i.e. by assuming the trim they did not verify. At trim=0, `possible[i] = min(241, i+1)` IS the true maximum count of the trailing-241-day window at full-view index i, so there is no systematic loosening and no escaping cohort.

The only name never flagged at trim=0 is one trading on 20180102 itself — which is information-theoretically undatable (the cube has no earlier data, and the reporter's own formula also returns 0 days for it). That is exactly what the code comment on lines 97-98 documents.

Secondary claim (`scripts/anatomy.py:106`) also does not hold as described. The line numbers are right, but with trim=0 `full_px[:20]` is the first 20 trading days of the view (2018-01-02..~2018-01-30), not "warm-up + 20 days", so the mislabelled set is only IPOs inside that 20-day window — not "2017年末到2018年初上市的那批票". More importantly it is a deliberate tolerance, not an oversight: `seen = np.cumsum(np.isfinite(full_px))` (line 105) cannot distinguish "listed before the data begins" from "listed on day 0" at all, so some day-0 tolerance is mandatory. The reporter's suggested fix ("在含 warm-up 的视图第一天就有价格") is a no-op at trim=0 and, read as "require a price on view day 1", is strictly worse: it would stamp `age = seen` on every name that was suspended on 2018-01-02 and so classify it as 上市不足250日 for its first 250 days — in A-shares at the start of 2018 that halted set is far larger than the January-2018 IPO cohort. Either way the magnitude is bounded by ~20-40 names × <=250 days (<=1e4 cells) against a bucket that is 7.088% of ~5e6 labelled cells (~3.5e5 cells), i.e. <=3% of the bucket, which cannot move the −28.7% segment excess enough to change the h_K_ex_both argument.

Forward-looking caveat only (not a current defect): if the store is ever rebuilt with pre-2018 history, or if `START` in `idea_search.py` is ever moved off the store's first day, `possible` would then need `+ ps.trim`. Today `ps.trim == 0` and the line is correct.
